sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Hip Thrust Bench is a machine-based exercise that targets the glutes through a horizontal hip extension movement.

Using a dedicated hip thrust bench provides a stable and comfortable platform, allowing you to focus entirely on driving through the hips.

This exercise is one of the most effective movements for building glute strength, size, and power, and is widely used by athletes and bodybuilders alike.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Maximises glute activation compared to most other exercises
- Dedicated bench provides stability and consistent positioning
- Reduces lower back strain by supporting the upper body
- Allows for heavy loading to build glute strength and size
- Improves hip extension power for athletic performance
- Enhances posterior chain development
- Supports progressive overload easily with barbell loading

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Glutes (Gluteus Maximus)

Secondary: Hamstrings, Quadriceps, Hip Adductors, Core

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Sit on the floor with your back against the edge of the hip thrust bench.
2. Position yourself so the pad sits around your shoulder blade height.
3. Roll a loaded barbell across your hips.
4. Place your feet flat on the floor, roughly shoulder-width apart.
5. Grip the barbell with both hands to keep it stable.
6. Start in a hip hinge position with your hips lowered toward the floor.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Maintaining a neutral spine and with your hands gripping the barbell, press the barbell up using your hips.
2. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.
3. Your back should remain straight throughout the movement — only bend at the hips.
4. At the top, your shins should be vertical and your torso parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the weight back down into the hip hinged position with control.
6. Repeat for reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Overextending the lower back at the top of the movement
- Feet placed too far forward or too close to the body
- Not driving through the heels
- Letting the knees cave inward
- Rushing the eccentric (lowering) phase
- Bar not centred on the hips, causing imbalance
- Not achieving full hip extension at the top
- Placing back too high or too low on the bench pad

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Hip Thrust Bench / Dedicated Glute Bench
- Olympic Barbell (45 lbs / 20 kg)
- Weight Plates
- Optional: Barbell Pad or Hip Thrust Pad for comfort
- Optional: Resistance Band around the knees for added glute activation

sections.heading: Bench & Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Position the hip thrust bench so it is stable and won't slide.
2. Sit on the floor with the bench behind you.
3. Lean your upper back against the bench pad at shoulder blade height.
4. Roll the loaded barbell over your legs into your hip crease.
5. Place feet flat on the floor, roughly shoulder-width apart.
6. Toes can point slightly outward for comfort.
7. Grip the bar to stabilise it across your hips.

sections.heading: Foot Placement
sections.content:
1. Feet should be roughly shoulder-width apart.
2. Position feet so that at the top of the movement, shins are vertical.
3. If feet are too far forward, hamstrings take over.
4. If feet are too close, quads take over.
5. Toes angled slightly out (15-30 degrees) can improve comfort.
6. Drive through your heels to maximise glute engagement.
7. Experiment with foot position to find maximum glute activation.
8. Keep feet flat throughout the movement.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Barbell Hip Thrust (flat bench): Same movement on a standard flat bench
- Bodyweight Hip Thrust: Unloaded version for beginners
- Glute Bridge: Floor-based variation with shorter range of motion
- Single-Leg Hip Thrust: Unilateral variation for imbalance correction
- Cable Pull-Through: Hip hinge pattern using cable machine
- Kettlebell Swing: Explosive hip extension movement

sections.heading: Hip Thrust Variations
sections.content:
Barbell Hip Thrust Bench: Standard loaded hip thrust on dedicated bench
Banded Hip Thrust: Adding resistance band around knees for adductor engagement
Single-Leg Hip Thrust: Unilateral focus for balance and imbalance correction
Pause Hip Thrust: Hold at the top for 2-3 seconds for extra glute activation
Foot-Elevated Hip Thrust: Feet on a raised surface for increased range of motion
Smith Machine Hip Thrust: Machine-guided bar for consistent bar path

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
No Hip Thrust Bench: Use a standard flat bench or sturdy box
Lower Back Pain: Focus on posterior pelvic tilt at the top, avoid hyperextension
Knee Discomfort: Adjust foot placement, try wider or narrower stance
Bar Discomfort on Hips: Use a thick barbell pad or folded towel
No Barbell Available: Use dumbbells, kettlebells, or a resistance band
Beginner: Start with bodyweight glute bridges and progress to loaded hip thrusts
